approval_timeline.complex: About 28 days for initial plan review in Phoenix, longer if corrections are issued or if the TI requires multiple disciplines and resubmittals.
approval_timeline.simple: Commercial TI/addition/remodel scopes usually require plan review; expect at least several business days to a few weeks depending on completeness, valuation, and local queue.

checklist: Verify your contractor license is current and valid in AZ
Confirm your liability insurance is active (certificate is conditional only when the listed condition applies at permit office)
Have the property address and legal parcel number ready
Know the project value/cost — required on most permit applications
ADA fixture counts per IBC Table 2902.1 (1 toilet + 1 lavatory per 1–25 occupants per sex; verify current edition)
Demising wall fire-rated assembly between tenants per IBC 706.3 (1-hour typical; 2-hour for higher-occupancy adjacencies)
Accessible-parking ratio per IBC 1106 + 1106.4 (1 per 25 spaces; 1 of every 6 must be van-accessible)
Exit access travel distance ≤200 ft (sprinklered) / ≤75 ft (non-sprinklered) per IBC 1017
Sprinkler head additions or relocations: hydraulic recalc + permit + 5-year cert update per NFPA 13/25
Lighting power density per IECC C405 (e.g. ≤0.79 W/sf for open-plan office)
Mechanical zoning per IMC 403 with tenant-controlled VAV / ductless on each occupied space
Fire alarm initiating-device coordination with base building (smoke detectors at HVAC return per NFPA 72 §17.7)
Accessible route from accessible entrance to all tenant areas per ADA §206 — no thresholds >½ in unbeveled
Means of egress: 2 exits required if occupant load >49 OR travel distance exceeds limits per IBC 1006
Energy code envelope + windows + insulation comply with IECC C402 if exterior wall is touched
Asbestos / lead survey for buildings pre-1980 if disturbing partitions, ceilings, or flooring
Glass + glazing: safety glazing per IBC 2406 in any pane within 24 in of doors or 60 in of floor

Confirm the required license is active and matches the application: Arizona ROC-licensed contractor pulls the permit — the contractor's ROC license number must appear on the application. Phoenix also requires separate City Contractor Registration on top of the ROC license before the permit will be accepted.
Bring 2 copies of all documents to City of Phoenix Planning & Development Department (PDD)
response_body.city_contractor_registration: Phoenix requires separate City Contractor Registration in addition to the Arizona ROC license. Verify the registration is current before submitting the permit; an expired city registration will block the application. Renewal is handled through City of Phoenix contractor registration processes.

common_mistakes: Submitting the permit application without verifying current Phoenix contractor registration status — an expired or lapsed city registration will block your application silently. Verify your registration is current BEFORE submitting.
Trying to split this into separate residential-style trade permits instead of using Phoenix's commercial TI permit process and combined review path.
Closing ceilings or walls before the electrical and mechanical rough-in inspections are approved.
Not showing diffuser relocation on the mechanical sheets, which can trigger corrections at plan review.
Understating the project valuation on a $95,000 commercial TI — Phoenix can reject or revalue the permit.
Submitting partition plans without reflected ceiling, sprinkler, alarm/strobe, diffuser/return, and emergency-lighting coordination.
Forgetting commercial energy-code forms for lighting controls, occupancy sensors, daylight zones, HVAC controls, or envelope/glazing changes.
Leaving low-voltage/data/security/access-control out of the permit set or ignoring plenum-rated cable, firestopping, and controlled-door egress release requirements.
Assuming existing restrooms and reception counters are acceptable without verifying accessible route, door clearances, hardware, signage, and path-of-travel obligations.

response_body.inspection_booking: Schedule inspections through the City of Phoenix PDD/Accela online portal. Phoenix requires a minimum 24-hour advance notice; same-day requests are not accepted. Phone: (602) 262-7811. Use the Phoenix permit portal and request the specific inspection type tied to the commercial TI permit.

inspections.description: Inspector checks non-load-bearing partition layout, wall framing attachment, fireblocking where required, door openings, and that no structural members were altered without approval.
inspections.timing: After framing is complete and before drywall is installed

inspections.description: Inspector verifies receptacle and lighting rough-in locations, box fill, cable/conduit support, circuit labeling, GFCI/AFCI where applicable, and that any new circuits match the approved plans.
inspections.timing: Before walls or ceilings are closed

inspections.description: Inspector checks diffuser relocation, duct routing changes, air distribution balance impacts, access to dampers, and that any modified ductwork is supported and sealed properly.
inspections.timing: Before ceiling closure or concealment of mechanical work

inspections.description: Inspector verifies all partitions, lighting, receptacles, diffuser locations, ceiling finishes, exit paths, and life-safety items match the approved permit set and that the space is ready for occupancy.
inspections.timing: After all work is complete and before tenant occupancy

inspections: Building rough/final — verify demising partitions, rated assemblies, firestopping, doors/hardware, egress, accessibility, and CO/suite conditions.
Electrical rough/final — verify lighting layout, controls, emergency lighting, exit signs, panels, receptacles, and equipment schedules.
Mechanical rough/final or air-balance verification — confirm HVAC zoning, ventilation, diffuser/return layout, thermostat locations, transfer air, and TAB report if required.
Low-voltage / data / access-control inspection if required — verify cable routing, plenum ratings, firestopping, card-reader egress releases, and fire-alarm interface.
Fire alarm / sprinkler acceptance test if partitions, ceilings, notification appliances, duct detectors, or sprinkler heads changed.

pro_tips: Check your Phoenix contractor registration renewal date before starting any permit application — registration lapses are the #1 avoidable rejection reason.
Phoenix uses a single-permit system for many trade combos, so confirm whether your TI can be processed under one commercial building permit package instead of separate trade permits.
Submit a clean reflected ceiling plan with lighting and diffuser locations up front; that avoids back-and-forth on the mechanical and electrical review.
Have the ROC license and city registration ready before opening the portal so you do not lose time at intake.
For commercial TI work, include the valuation breakdown and tenant finish scope in the first submittal to reduce correction cycles.

Treat office TI as a building/MEP/fire/accessibility coordination job: demising partitions, ceiling/lighting, HVAC zoning, low-voltage/data, ADA path-of-travel, and fire alarm/sprinkler drawings can each drive separate reviews.
Get existing reflected ceiling, sprinkler, fire alarm, HVAC diffuser/return, and low-voltage pathways before pricing — moving walls without these backgrounds creates change orders.
Confirm landlord/building engineer requirements early for after-hours work, fire-life-safety shutdowns, low-voltage pathways, air-balance reports, and certificate-of-occupancy signoff.

warnings: Commercial scope may require companion reviews/permits not fully proven here: electrical, mechanical, plumbing.
Some report claims do not yet have quoted source snippets; use the listed building department source before relying on them.
watch_out: Generic office TI answers often miss low-voltage/data permits, fire alarm/sprinkler deferred submittals, and HVAC balancing; those can delay tenant move-in even when the building permit is issued.
New demising walls or conference rooms can break existing egress, strobe visibility, sprinkler spacing, return-air paths, and ventilation assumptions.
ADA path-of-travel and restroom work can be required even when the office remodel feels mostly cosmetic; document the 20% disproportionality analysis if applicable.
what_to_bring: Completed commercial TI permit application and project address
Arizona ROC license number and current City of Phoenix contractor registration
Two or more plan sets showing partition layout, reflected ceiling plan, lighting, receptacles, and diffuser locations
Code summary and occupant load / egress information if the TI affects layout
Owner authorization or tenant authorization letter if the contractor is filing on behalf of the tenant
response_body.zoning_hoa_flag: HOA restrictions are usually not the issue for an interior commercial office TI, but zoning and occupancy approvals can still matter if the work changes use, occupant load, or egress. If the suite is in a historic district or has a special zoning overlay, additional review may apply.
